questions.title: What is the difference between covariance and correlation, and when do you normalise?
Pearson or Spearman, and why might they disagree?
How do you check a correlation before you trust it?

anchors.text: Missing, wrong or unrelated to the question.
Partly there, with the key point muddled or absent.
Right and clear, with only small gaps.
Right, precise and complete, with nothing to correct.

dimensions.title: Accuracy
dimensions.question: Is the core claim correct and specific?

anchors.text: The claim is wrong, vague, or missing.
The idea is there but muddled, or a fact is wrong.
The core idea is correct and stated plainly. Minor gaps are fine.
Correct and precise, with the key formula or fact and no slips.

dimensions.title: Structure
dimensions.question: Does it follow the 60-second shape: direct answer, the reason, then where it is used?

anchors.text: No clear shape. It wanders.
Some order, but the answer comes late or the reason is missing.
Direct answer first, then a reason, then a use. Easy to follow.
The same shape, tight, and the follow-ups it invites are anticipated.

dimensions.title: Trade-offs
dimensions.question: Does it name caveats: when it breaks, what it costs, and what it is compared with?

anchors.text: No caveat, or the caveat is wrong.
One caveat, stated without a condition or cost.
At least one real caveat with the condition under which it applies.
Caveats with their conditions, costs and a stated alternative.

dimensions.title: Communication
dimensions.question: Is it concise, plain and calm, with jargon used only where it helps?

anchors.text: Hard to follow, or padded with jargon.
Understandable, but long or hedged throughout.
Concise and plain. A senior colleague would follow it without effort.
Concise, plain and confident. Each sentence earns its place.
